items.title: FPL GW4 EXPERT Wildcard Team & Transfer Trends! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 4 Team Plans
items.headline: Cole Palmer dominates Gameweek 4 plans as experts overhaul squads on Wildcards
items.summary:
Gameweek 4 brings a major expert-led reshuffle, with 35% of the 100 surveyed managers activating a Wildcard and a further 2% using a Free Hit. Only 11% make no move, while most non-chip managers target Chelsea and Arsenal assets. Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa are the overwhelming free-transfer priorities, while Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Rayan Cherki, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are among the most common sales ahead of the Manchester derby.

Palmer is the defining pick of the week. He appears in every one of the 35 expert Wildcard drafts and is also captained by 70% of the sample for Chelsea's home fixture against Hull City. João Pedro is the clear fallback captain at 18%, while Erling Haaland receives only 8% backing despite his usual premium appeal. All of the experts using Triple Captain place it on Palmer, although only 4% of the overall group deploy the chip, suggesting many still prefer to save it for a later high-upside week.

The Wildcard template is built around Palmer, Rogers, João Pedro and Haaland, with Riccardo Calafiori and Konsa virtually universal defensive selections at 97% each. Egan-Riley is the preferred £4.0m defender, while Muharemovic and Lewis Hall provide popular additional options. In goal, Kinsky leads the way, ahead of David Raya and Verbruggen, generally paired with a £4.0m reserve. The key Arsenal structure is Calafiori and Konsa plus either Saka or Raya; Saka is marginally more popular, but the Raya-and-Morgan Gibbs-White alternative offers a similarly priced route.

Midfield choices beyond Palmer and Rogers are less settled. Gross is selected in around two-thirds of Wildcards, while Saka, Gibbs-White and Gakpo are viable alternatives. Experts are notably cooler on Gakpo than the wider FPL market: despite being the most-bought player overall, he is included in only 26% of Wildcards, partly because Liverpool's schedule stiffens after Fulham in Gameweek 4. Up front, the third striker slot is the main compromise: Wissa remains the most common choice but falls sharply from his previous near-essential status, with Barry and Gonzalo competing as cheaper alternatives. Bruno Fernandes is in only 9% of Wildcards, underlining the willingness to move away from Manchester United assets for the upcoming fixture swing.
key_points: Cole Palmer is in 100% of expert Wildcards and is the captaincy favourite for Chelsea at home to Hull City, backed by 70% of experts.
Palmer is the only Triple Captain pick in the survey, but just 4% of experts use the chip in Gameweek 4.
Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa join Palmer as the standout non-Wildcard transfer targets.
Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Rayan Cherki, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are major sales as managers reduce Manchester exposure before the derby.
Riccardo Calafiori and Konsa are selected by 97% of Wildcard teams, with Egan-Riley the preferred budget defender.
João Pedro and Erling Haaland are in 100% and 97% respectively of expert Wildcards; the third forward is split between Wissa, Barry and Gonzalo.
Experts show limited enthusiasm for Cody Gakpo despite his popularity in the wider market, with only 26% selecting him on a Wildcard.
The main Arsenal decision is Saka versus Raya: Saka is slightly more popular, while Raya can fund a midfield alternative such as Morgan Gibbs-White.

items.headline: Wildcard draft for Gameweek 4 backs Arsenal defensive triple-up and João Pedro captaincy
items.summary:
A Gameweek 4 Wildcard draft prioritises defensive value, led by David Raya and an intended triple-up on Arsenal’s back line. Calvin Bassey is included for his attacking potential, while Ibrahima Konaté is viewed as underpriced at £4.4m. The trade-off is that three Arsenal defensive slots prevent investment in Arsenal attackers such as Bukayo Saka, Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz, but Arsenal’s defensive outlook is considered strong enough to justify it. Joël Veltman is another attacking-minded defensive option, with Coventry away next, while Malick Thiaw and John Egan provide cheap bench cover for favourable upcoming fixtures.

Midfield is built around flexibility rather than immediately owning Bruno Fernandes. Bryan Mbeumo earns a place after scoring in each of the previous two matches, while Cole Palmer is preferred to Morgan Rogers because his price point makes future moves to premium midfielders easier. Palmer can be sold to reach Bruno Fernandes or Saka in the coming weeks without requiring a major squad restructure. Pascal Groß and Morgan Gibbs-White complete the main midfield options, with Gibbs-White particularly appealing for matches against Aston Villa, Coventry and Crystal Palace over the next three gameweeks; Sangaré is retained as a bench option.

Erling Haaland and João Pedro are treated as near-essential forwards, especially in a structure that excludes Bruno Fernandes. Yoane Wissa completes the attack. Captaincy is placed on João Pedro, with Palmer as vice-captain, reflecting the desire to target Chelsea’s attacking potential in Gameweek 4. Managers who have already made transfers can still activate the Wildcard later in the week, with those free transfers restored for Gameweek 5.

Calvin Bassey is selected for attacking threat, while Ibrahima Konaté is considered excellent value at £4.4m.

items.headline: Haaland anchors a Gameweek 4 Wildcard built around Chelsea’s fixture run
items.summary:

Haaland is viewed as the standout captain in most weeks, while Cole Palmer and João Pedro are joined by Rogers to exploit Chelsea’s favourable fixtures. The logic is that Chelsea’s players are strong picks individually, their schedule is worth targeting despite recent clean sheets, and the lack of European commitments improves their long-term minutes prospects.

The goalkeeper combination is Bart Verbruggen and Antonín Kinský, offering rotation rather than the more expensive set-and-forget route of David Raya. Raya remains an attractive option, but avoiding him allows investment in three Arsenal assets elsewhere. His price also creates useful flexibility, as he can be moved to most premium or mid-priced midfielders if plans change. Pascal Groß fills the final midfield place at £5.5m as a value option, while Yoane Wissa keeps the forward line affordable ahead of a better fixture run despite a disappointing Gameweek 3.

Lewis Hall and Neco Williams provide bench attacking upside, while Slater is the £4.5m midfield enabler who can cover minutes when required. If extra funds are needed, Wissa can be downgraded to Barry at Everton, but the preferred version retains Wissa for his upcoming fixtures.

Haaland and João Pedro lead the forward line, viewed as two of the league’s most prolific strikers, while Alexander Isak is acknowledged as a possible alternative in that conversation.

The goalkeeper selection is Kinski, based on the belief that Tottenham’s defensive numbers have been stronger than widely recognised since De Zerbi’s arrival. Apart from the Brentford match, Spurs are judged to have looked solid enough to make their goalkeeper a worthwhile wildcard pick. The defence includes Calafiori and Konsa, described as a double-Arsenal defensive pairing, alongside Vuskovic and Meharemovic as budget defenders with defensive-contribution potential who rotate well over upcoming gameweeks.

Palmer and Saka provide the premium midfield spending, while Dominik Szoboszlai and Pascal Gross are the value options. Gross is rated the standout midfielder at £5.5m, giving the squad a route to returns without sacrificing the two elite midfield picks. The structure is therefore heavily weighted towards Haaland, Palmer and Saka, but still leaves room for João Pedro and mid-priced midfield coverage.

The bench is planned around future fixtures rather than immediate returns. A £4.0m goalkeeper keeps costs down, while Tavernier and Lewis Hall are considered useful options for later gameweeks. Gonzalo is deliberately benched until Gameweek 6, when he begins a run of three consecutive matches against newly promoted teams. This remains a first wildcard draft rather than a final squad, with the main risk being that several cheaper picks are selected for rotation or future fixture value rather than immediate starts.

João Pedro joins Haaland up front, with Isak noted as another forward capable of competing with them for output.
Kinski is selected in goal because Tottenham’s underlying defensive form is rated highly despite the Brentford setback.

items.title: My transfer tips ahead of Gameweek 4 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Sell Foden, back Rogers and target Palmer before Gameweek 4
items.summary:
Phil Foden is the priority sale after being benched in Gameweek 3, with Manchester City’s midfield rotation making him too expensive a risk. Rayan Cherki is less urgent to move on because he starts the previous match and faces Manchester United next, a defence that has not looked secure. Even so, Cherki’s long-term minutes remain difficult to trust.

Morgan Rogers is the standout midfield target, with Hull at home next and a favourable enough run beyond that. Bryan Mbeumo is viable either as a hold or a sale to fund Rogers: his minutes remain strong while Amad is unavailable, but managers wanting the Aston Villa midfielder can make the switch. Morgan Gibbs-White is another appealing higher-priced option, particularly with Coventry at home in Gameweek 5 and penalty duties. Bruno Fernandes remains a reliable asset, but moving from Fernandes to Cole Palmer is preferred this week because Palmer offers stronger upside while releasing budget elsewhere.

Thierno Barry is a value forward at £5.6m, with Everton lacking another recognised striker and facing Ipswich at home in Gameweek 5 followed by Hull away in Gameweek 6. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a reasonable Wildcard sale, but non-Wildcard managers can hold because he has two home matches across the next two Gameweeks and generally secure minutes. In Liverpool’s attack, do not rush to sell Dominik Szoboszlai or Florian Wirtz before Fulham at home. Cody Gakpo looks the best long-term Liverpool forward option due to his ability to play on either wing or through the middle when Alexander Isak is rested. Isak is attractive at £9.1m, but Champions League football is likely to bring more managed minutes and the favourable Ipswich fixture has already passed.
key_points: Sell Phil Foden after his Gameweek 3 benching, as Manchester City rotation makes his minutes too uncertain.
Rayan Cherki can be held for Manchester United next after starting in Gameweek 3, but he is not a dependable long-term minutes pick.
Morgan Rogers is the leading midfield transfer target ahead of Hull at home and a decent fixture run.
Bryan Mbeumo remains a good hold while Amad is absent, although selling him for Rogers is a valid move.
Cole Palmer is preferred to Bruno Fernandes this week, with the transfer also freeing funds.
Thierno Barry is a £5.6m forward target because Everton have limited striker alternatives and face Ipswich and Hull in Gameweeks 5 and 6.
Hold Dominic Calvert-Lewin outside of a Wildcard because of two upcoming home fixtures and solid expected minutes.
Avoid hasty Liverpool sales before Fulham at home; Cody Gakpo is favoured over Alexander Isak long term because Isak may be managed around Champions League matches.

items.title: FREE HIT ACTIVE 🚨 | THE FPL WATCHLIST GW4 🔎 | PALMER, KONSA & GAKPO 🎯 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Cole Palmer edges João Pedro as the Gameweek 4 captaincy call against Hull
items.summary:
Gameweek 4 centres on Chelsea’s home fixture against Hull, with Cole Palmer and João Pedro the standout captaincy options. Hull arrive with clean sheets but have conceded five big chances and rank only 14th for expected goals conceded, having faced low-scoring Villa and Coventry sides. Chelsea’s attack is viewed as a major step up in quality, making a heavy home win plausible. Palmer is preferred to João Pedro for captaincy because of his penalty duties, midfielder scoring and 20-point haul potential, although João Pedro remains close and is considered a near-essential Chelsea attacker.

A Chelsea attacking triple-up is attractive on a Free Hit for Hull at home, with Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers the preferred combination. It is less appealing as a Wildcard structure because Chelsea then face Brentford away, Bournemouth, Everton away and Spurs, while Palmer has not yet established himself as a reliable talisman. Palmer and João Pedro are the recommended longer-term pair. Chelsea’s defence remains difficult to trust after a long clean-sheet drought: Martinez is the only realistic Wildcard option, while Laqua is expensive and Hato, Gusto and Reece James carry rotation or minutes concerns.

Arsenal offer the clearer defensive investment. Ezri Kza, priced at £4.4m, is the leading budget defender after starting ahead of the absent Moscara and delivering both DefCon potential and some attacking involvement. His minutes carry some medium-term risk when competition returns, but Arsenal clean-sheet points alone justify the gamble. Calafiori is seen as close to undroppable when fit, while Raya, Gabriel and Kza make a viable triple defensive Arsenal stack. Bukayo Saka is a good player with penalties while Yarez is absent, but the panel questions whether he is worth the premium over cheaper midfielders and Arsenal defenders; his main value is flexibility to move back to Bruno Fernandes.

Liverpool attackers remain strong Gameweek 4 targets against a struggling Fulham defence. Alexander Isak and Gakpo have upside, but Isak’s managed minutes and injury history make him a risk in a Champions League schedule, while Gakpo has reportedly missed training as a precaution and may face competition for starts. A Free Hit can justify a Liverpool attacking triple-up, but managers without one are advised not to force transfers for them. Erling Haaland remains a safe captain against Manchester United, though João Pedro or Palmer are favoured by some due to Chelsea’s superior fixture.

The transfer theme is restraint. One manager rolls with a viable squad rather than spend another early chip, while another uses a Free Hit to load up on Chelsea, Liverpool and Arsenal. Moving Bruno Fernandes or Bryan Mbeumo out for Chelsea midfielders is not automatically endorsed: Bruno has Fulham next, Mbeumo remains worth starting against Manchester City, and managers should avoid using transfers merely to chase last week’s returns. A Gameweek 6 Wildcard is preferred to an unnecessary Gameweek 4 reset for squads already carrying Palmer, Arsenal coverage and playable forwards.
key_points: Captain Cole Palmer against Hull if chasing Chelsea’s highest ceiling; João Pedro is the main alternative, while Haaland remains the safe pick against Manchester United.
Buy Ezri Kza at £4.4m if a defensive transfer is needed, with Arsenal clean-sheet potential outweighing the future risk from Moscara’s return.
A Wildcard Arsenal triple-up can be Raya, Calafiori and Kza/Gabriel, with the panel preferring defensive certainty to forcing Saka at his premium price.
Use Palmer and João Pedro as the preferred long-term Chelsea pair; reserve a third Chelsea attacker for a Gameweek 4 Free Hit rather than a permanent Wildcard slot.
Avoid Chelsea defenders beyond Martinez unless chasing a short-term punt: Laqua is costly, while Hato, Gusto and Reece James have uncertain minutes.
Liverpool’s Isak and Gakpo are strong Free Hit options against Fulham, but Isak’s fitness management and Gakpo’s training absence make permanent transfer moves less straightforward.
Do not sell Bruno Fernandes or Bryan Mbeumo simply to chase Chelsea assets, especially with Bruno facing Fulham next and Mbeumo still worth starting against City.
Managers with stable squads are encouraged to roll transfers and target a Gameweek 6 Wildcard rather than burn more chips early.

items.title: TRIPLE CAPTAIN ACTIVE! 🚨 MY FPL GW4 TEAM ✅
items.headline: Cole Palmer Triple Captain backed for Chelsea’s Gameweek 4 meeting with Hull
items.summary:
A 40-point opening week after the wildcard produces a sharp red arrow, with Trevoh Chalobah’s own goal, yellow cards and widespread blanks compounding the damage. However, the underlying squad structure remains intact and there is no panic over the poor return: the pre-wildcard side also blanks heavily, while the current team retains a strong spread of premium attackers, Arsenal defensive cover and playable bench options.

The Gameweek 4 XI is Raya; Van Hecke, De Cuyper and Konsa; Saka, Foden, Szoboszlai and Gross; Haaland, Wissa and Joao Pedro. Raya is preferred despite his £6.0m price because Arsenal lead the clean-sheet projections at 50%, while Konsa looks increasingly secure for Aston Villa after returning to the starting side. De Cuyper offers attacking upside from set pieces and an advanced role, while Van Hecke remains a reliable cheaper defender. Wissa starts despite a difficult trip to Leeds because none of the bench options is more appealing.

The decisive move is Foden to Cole Palmer, funded by £3.3m in the bank, with Palmer handed the triple-captain armband for Chelsea at home to Hull. Manchester City attackers are considered too difficult to trust beyond Haaland because rotation is likely, while Palmer has the week’s best projected goal total in a fixture that looks better than Hull’s three opening clean sheets suggest. Hull have conceded more than five expected goals, the 13th-worst record in the league, so their defensive record is viewed as unsustainable. Joao Pedro becomes vice-captain, while Haaland remains a perfectly viable ordinary captain against Manchester United given his eight goals and three assists in seven derbies.

The chip call also reflects doubts over later triple-captain alternatives. Haaland at home to Ipswich in Gameweek 7 carries a potential rotation concern after Liverpool and PSG, while Bruno Fernandes at home to Coventry in Gameweek 14 depends on Manchester United improving and surviving the Champions League schedule. The plan is to roll transfers in Gameweeks 5 and 6, then potentially replace De Cuyper in Gameweek 7 with Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi if minutes become uncertain. Longer term, a Gameweek 8 move away from Haaland is under consideration, freeing funds to build a midfield around Palmer, Saka, Bruno Fernandes and other penalty-taking assets, but Haaland is retained for now.
key_points: Transfer Foden out for Cole Palmer in Gameweek 4, using £3.3m in the bank.
Triple-captain Palmer against Hull, with Joao Pedro as vice-captain.
Haaland is a strong standard captain option against Manchester United but is not preferred over Palmer’s home fixture.
Raya, Konsa and Arsenal’s clean-sheet projection support retaining expensive Arsenal defensive cover.
Hull’s three clean sheets are viewed as unsustainable after conceding more than five expected goals in three matches.
Plan to roll transfers in Gameweeks 5 and 6 unless De Cuyper’s minutes become a concern.
A potential Gameweek 7 defensive switch is De Cuyper to Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi, whose favourable run begins with Sunderland at home.
A longer-term Haaland exit around Gameweek 8 could fund a premium midfield featuring Palmer, Saka and Bruno Fernandes.

items.title: BEST 3x ARSENAL IN FPL NOW? 👀 🔴 Saka vs Konsa!  @FPLRaptor  #fpl #premierleague #football #arsenał
items.headline: Saka offers Arsenal upside, but triple defence remains the Wildcard safety play
items.summary:
Arsenal’s defensive strength makes a double-up feel close to essential on a Wildcard, with Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa presented as the standout value routes. Calafiori is effectively playing with the attacking licence of a midfielder, having already had a Gameweek 3 goal ruled out, so his appeal does not rely solely on clean sheets. Konsa’s £4.4m price makes him an extremely cheap way into the Arsenal back line.

The main Wildcard decision is the third Arsenal slot. David Raya offers the safest route: a reliable stream of clean sheets with occasional save points, alongside Calafiori and Konsa. The concern is whether Raya at £6.0m is worth the premium over a £4.5m goalkeeper such as Bart Verbruggen, while Gabriel at £8.0m is difficult to accommodate.

A more aggressive structure is double Arsenal defence plus one attacker, with Bukayo Saka the preferred high-ceiling option. Saka has scored in the opening gameweeks, carries potential penalty responsibility depending on the line-up, and offers the explosive returns that a third defender cannot match. Martin Odegaard is also attracting interest after returning to form at a relatively affordable price, while William Saliba improves in Gameweek 3 after an underwhelming Gameweek 2 and remains another defensive consideration.

Saka’s price is also useful for squad flexibility: if he fails to justify the investment, he can be downgraded easily to almost any midfield alternative, including a route back to Bruno Fernandes. The lean is currently Calafiori, Konsa and Saka, balancing Arsenal’s defensive security with attacking upside. The alternative is to lock in triple Arsenal defence, avoid future selection headaches and potentially hold the unit for much of the season, but that comes at the cost of access to a crowded pool of strong attackers.
key_points: Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa are viewed as near-lock Wildcard picks for a double Arsenal defensive investment.
Calafiori offers attacking upside beyond clean sheets, having had a goal disallowed in Gameweek 3 despite early substitutions.
David Raya is the safest third Arsenal pick, but his £6.0m cost is questioned against £4.5m options such as Bart Verbruggen.
Bukayo Saka is the preferred third Arsenal slot for managers chasing upside, with early goals, potential penalties and a high ceiling.
Saka’s price makes future moves easy, as he can be downgraded to most midfielders or used to return to Bruno Fernandes.
Triple Arsenal defence is the conservative route and could be held long term, but it limits access to other strong attacking options.

items.title: GAKPO AND ISAK LOOK LIKE GREAT FPL PICKS  ⚽️ FUL (H) in GW4 👀  @FPLRaptor #fpl #premierleague
items.headline: Isak and Gakpo emerge as Liverpool’s best Fulham punts in Gameweek 4
items.summary:
Liverpool’s home match against Fulham in Gameweek 4 stands out as one of the strongest alternatives to the Chelsea-Haaland fixture. Fulham concede heavily early in the season and are viewed as one of the league’s weakest defences, making this an attractive one-week entry point for Liverpool attackers.

Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo are preferred over Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz on both the eye test and underlying data. Liverpool are expected to keep creating high-quality chances under Andoni Iraola’s attacking approach, as his Bournemouth teams do, but Isak and Gakpo currently look like the most convincing routes into those chances. Gakpo appears relatively secure for minutes, while Isak is the standout target for managers buying now or activating a Wildcard.

The main caution is Liverpool’s fixture swing immediately after Fulham. Their run includes Bournemouth, Manchester City, Brentford, Brighton and Arsenal, with Arsenal leading the league for expected goals conceded, City second and Brentford also posting strong defensive numbers. Brighton looks a potentially exploitable fixture, but the overall schedule is not strong enough to make Liverpool attackers automatic long-term holds.

Managers who already own Szoboszlai may reasonably keep him, particularly because of his reliable minutes and possible penalty involvement, rather than using a transfer or chip to chase another Liverpool option. For new buyers, however, Gameweek 4 is the time to act: Isak is the preferred signing, Gakpo is a viable alternative, and managers who pass on Liverpool this week may be better served looking elsewhere unless they are building a Haaland-free squad.
key_points: Liverpool at home to Fulham in Gameweek 4 is a prime attacking fixture because Fulham are among the weakest defences so far.
Alexander Isak is the preferred Liverpool buy for managers making a transfer or playing a Wildcard.
Cody Gakpo is also an appealing option, with strong recent performances and relatively secure minutes.
Dominik Szoboszlai remains a reasonable hold for current owners due to his minutes and potential penalty duty.
Liverpool’s fixtures worsen after Fulham, with Manchester City, Brentford and Arsenal all presenting difficult defensive opposition.
Managers buying a Liverpool attacker should view Gameweek 4 as the key entry point rather than a long-term fixture run.

items.title: GW4 vs GW6 WILDCARD FOR FPL? 🍟 📝 @FPLRaptor  #fpl #premierleague #football #wildcard
items.headline: Gameweek 6 Wildcard remains the plan despite Gameweek 4 team-value pressure
items.summary:
The current preference is to save the Wildcard until Gameweek 6 rather than join the popular Gameweek 3 or 4 activation. Three early transfers have already been made for Gameweek 4, bringing in Pal Dardai, Mehammed Besic and Morgan Gibbs-White, with all three viewed as useful short-term picks ahead of the international break.

Gameweek 4 has appeal because the three-week international break creates uncertainty: injuries, rotation and changing form can quickly reshape squads, while a Wildcard restores flexibility through extra transfers. It also offers a route to increase exposure to Arsenal and Chelsea, two sides worth targeting but not currently owned heavily. Activating early could improve the immediate squad and help recover ground in team value.

However, Gameweek 4 is not considered an especially strong fixture-swing point, and the existing squad is already built to perform through Gameweeks 4 and 5. The downside of waiting is lower team value than managers who have already Wildcarded, but the benefit is more information before committing to a new structure. Unless a key player is injured or another major issue emerges in midweek, the plan is to resist the short-term value gain and hold the Wildcard for Gameweek 6.
key_points: The preferred Wildcard timing is Gameweek 6, not Gameweek 4, because the present squad is still well set for Gameweeks 4 and 5.
Pal Dardai, Mehammed Besic and Morgan Gibbs-White arrive as three early Gameweek 4 transfers for short-term value.
A Gameweek 4 Wildcard would allow increased investment in Arsenal and Chelsea, who are currently underrepresented in the squad.
The international break makes Gameweek 4 an attractive contingency Wildcard window because injuries and rotation can change plans quickly.
Lower team value is accepted as the cost of waiting, with extra information viewed as more valuable than chasing price rises.
A key midweek injury or other major squad problem could still trigger a Gameweek 4 Wildcard.

items.title: FPL GW4 Transfer Tips 🔥 SELL Bruno ❌ Palmer IN ✅
items.headline: Cole Palmer edges Morgan Rogers as Chelsea’s key Gameweek 4 target
items.summary:
Chelsea attack is the main Gameweek 4 target as Hull visit Stamford Bridge. Hull have started with three clean sheets, but that is too small a sample to conclude they are difficult to break down, while Chelsea have scored early in every match and look strong going forward. Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers are all viable additions, with Chelsea’s wider run also appealing: after Hull, they have Bournemouth, Spurs, Manchester United, Sunderland, Leeds and Crystal Palace, predominantly at home. That makes Chelsea players easier to hold through less attractive fixtures rather than forcing an immediate exit plan.

João Pedro remains the standout value forward at £7.7m, with 90-minute appearances in every match and ownership above 72%, but he is not considered essential if squad structure requires spending elsewhere. Between Palmer and Rogers, the deciding factor is captaincy. Palmer’s previous output, apparent penalty responsibility and higher ceiling make him the preferred captain in Chelsea’s home fixtures, notably Gameweeks 4, 6 and 8. Rogers is a strong cheaper alternative, particularly for managers retaining Bruno Fernandes; Fernandes plus Rogers is judged slightly preferable to Palmer plus Bryan Mbeumo. Any pair of the three Chelsea options works, but Palmer and João Pedro is the preferred combination.

Liverpool assets are holds rather than buys before Fulham at home. Mohamed Salah remains worth keeping because of penalties, set pieces, guaranteed minutes and multiple routes to points, even if his open-play threat can make ownership frustrating. Florian Wirtz is also worth holding for Fulham if already owned, but his falling price and lack of returns mean he is not a transfer target. Alexander Isak’s two-goal haul against Ipswich has created excessive hype: at £9.1m, he lacks penalties, is vulnerable to early substitutions once Champions League football begins and may require two transfers to acquire. He is a fine short-term option but not a priority over Bukayo Saka, who offers set pieces and penalty potential. Liverpool’s tougher upcoming stretch—Bournemouth away, Manchester City, Brentford away, Brighton and Arsenal—limits the appeal of new double or triple attack investment.

Arsenal’s defensive dominance makes two defenders the preferred minimum on a Wildcard, with triple defence still attractive. Martin Ødegaard at £6.6m is nevertheless a compelling alternative to Saka for managers who do not expect to captain Arsenal often; he is starting regularly, linking well with Kai Havertz and collecting bonus when he returns. Saka remains the superior Arsenal captain due to penalties, but Arsenal’s most obvious captaincy week is Hull at home in Gameweek 10, so Ødegaard’s value can outweigh that premium. Dominic Calvert-Lewin should be held for Newcastle and Crystal Palace at home, while Everton’s Thierno Barry is the standout cheap-forward target after Beto’s departure leaves him with improved minutes, possible penalties and a good run from Gameweek 5. Yoane Wissa is also a hold through Leeds, Hull and Coventry despite occasionally operating deeper, as his minutes and possible penalty role remain valuable.
key_points: Target Chelsea against Hull in Gameweek 4, with Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers all strong options for a favourable largely home-heavy fixture run.
Palmer is preferred over Rogers for managers wanting a reliable alternative captain, while João Pedro remains excellent value but is not compulsory at 72% ownership.
Hold Salah and Wirtz for Fulham at home if already owned, but avoid rushing into Liverpool attackers ahead of a tougher run beginning at Bournemouth away.
Do not chase Isak solely after his Ipswich haul: his £9.1m price, lack of penalties and possible Champions League minute management weaken his long-term appeal.
On a Gameweek 4 Wildcard, prioritise at least two Arsenal defenders; Ødegaard is a credible £6.6m attacking alternative if Saka captaincy is not central to the plan.
Keep Calvert-Lewin for home matches against Newcastle and Crystal Palace, as he has penalties, strong underlying chances and regular 90-minute potential.
Barry becomes a leading budget forward at £5.6m after Everton sell Beto without replacing him; he has improved security of starts and may inherit penalties.
Keep Wissa through Gameweek 6 rather than reacting to his deeper spells, with Leeds away, Hull at home and Coventry away still a useful run.

items.headline: João Pedro and Chelsea’s attack top the Gameweek 4 transfer agenda
items.summary:
João Pedro is the standout buy and a clear hold for Gameweek 4, with Chelsea hosting Hull before favourable matches against Bournemouth and Everton. Hull’s consecutive clean sheets mask poor defensive underlying numbers and weak opposition, while Chelsea’s attack has looked strong outside the Arsenal match. Cole Palmer is the premium midfield priority because he combines high shot volume with penalties and set pieces; Morgan Rogers is also attractive for his shooting and creativity, although a triple Chelsea attack carries some concentration risk. Erling Haaland remains a hold and a viable captain away to Manchester United, with Sunderland and Ipswich at home among Manchester City’s next four fixtures.

Liverpool assets also merit patience for Fulham at home. Mohamed Salah remains a non-negotiable hold despite recent sales, having come close to returns and retaining penalties, set pieces and open-play threat against a Fulham side that is vulnerable defensively. Alexander Isak is worth holding for Fulham, but is not worth major squad reconstruction after his two-goal haul against Ipswich, especially with Manchester City and Brentford to follow. Virgil van Dijk is similarly worth one more week for Fulham before becoming expendable. Bruno Fernandes is only a sell if downgrading him funds multiple upgrades; a single-transfer exit ahead of Manchester City is discouraged because Fulham away follows.

Among forwards, Barry at £5.6m and Fulham’s Gonzalo are the preferred medium-term purchases behind João Pedro. Barry is expected to play regularly as Everton’s available central forward, may have penalties and gets Ipswich and Hull in Gameweeks 5 and 6. Gonzalo has played 90 minutes in each match, posts strong shot numbers and potentially takes penalties, while Fulham face Ipswich, Hull and Coventry from Gameweeks 6 to 8. Yoane Wissa is a hold rather than a fresh buy: Newcastle’s chance creation has dipped, his penalty role and central position are less certain after Fernandez Pardo’s arrival, and he may face reduced minutes or a deeper role when Osula returns. Viktor Gyökeres is an urgent sale because he is not starting for Arsenal, while Mateta is injured and Watkins has left the Premier League.

Arsenal’s defence is the clearest route for defensive transfers. Conor is described as an exceptional £4.4m buy with Saliba absent until around Christmas, strong defensive-contribution potential and excellent clean-sheet fixtures against Sunderland, Leeds and Forest. Riccardo Calafiori is also a buy due to his advanced threat, apparent first-choice status and Arsenal’s elite defensive numbers. Leeds defender Maharovic is a cheaper differential with major defensive-contribution output and set-piece upside, though he needs rotating for Arsenal and Manchester United in Gameweeks 6 and 7. Avoid Sunderland defenders because of poor fixtures and rotation concerns, while Manchester City attackers other than Haaland are risky amid Champions League-driven rotation. Harvey Barnes and Elanga are also avoid calls: recent returns substantially exceed weak underlying numbers.
key_points: Captain João Pedro or Cole Palmer for Chelsea’s home match against Hull; Haaland away to Manchester United is the alternative premium captain.
Buy João Pedro immediately if absent, with Hull and Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge offering the strongest short-term fixtures.
Hold Salah for Fulham at home rather than switching to Cody Gakpo, whose long-term minutes become less secure after Liverpool’s new arrivals.
Prioritise Barry or Gonzalo as longer-term forward buys; Wissa is less appealing because Newcastle create little and his role may change.
Sell Gyökeres for lack of starts, Mateta because of injury, Watkins because he has left the Premier League, and Rodon because he is out until late October.
Buy Conor as Arsenal’s £4.4m defensive route while Saliba is sidelined; Calafiori is the higher-upside alternative.
Avoid non-Haaland Manchester City midfielders such as Cherki, Foden and Doku/Anjai because European and cup commitments increase rotation risk.
Keep Gabriel and Raya through Arsenal’s favourable fixture run, while Kinsky is the preferred £4.5m goalkeeper option.

items.headline: Ezre Concer offers cut-price Arsenal clean sheets, but rotation caps his appeal
items.summary:
Ezre Concer strengthens his case as a £4.4m route into Arsenal’s defence after starting in Gameweek 3 and collecting defensive-contribution points. Arsenal’s clean-sheet potential gives him a very high floor for his price, making him particularly attractive for managers using a Wildcard.

The main concern is security of starts. Mosca is absent from the squad, and his return to fitness could alter Concer’s place in the side. Arsenal also face Champions League commitments alongside Premier League matches, so fixture congestion increases the risk of rotation in defence.

There is also an opportunity-cost question over Arsenal’s three-player limit. Concer is far cheaper than Gabriel and David Raya, but selecting him as part of a defensive double-up or triple-up could prevent managers from buying Arsenal attackers. Solace has another assist, Odigard scores, and Bay Saka starts the season well, leaving several competing options for Arsenal slots.

Concer’s ceiling remains the reason not to treat him as an automatic buy. He has limited established attacking threat and defensive-contribution returns may not be regular, although his presence in the box against Chelsea offers some encouragement. He is not essential yet, but his price and Arsenal’s defensive strength make him a difficult player to ignore on a Gameweek 4 Wildcard.
key_points: Ezre Concer starts in Gameweek 3 and returns defensive-contribution points, enhancing his appeal at £4.4m.
Arsenal clean sheets give Concer a strong points floor, especially compared with more expensive options such as Gabriel and David Raya.
Mosca’s eventual return and Arsenal’s Champions League schedule create a meaningful rotation risk for Concer.
Concer has limited proven attacking upside, so his ceiling is lower than that of Arsenal’s more attacking defenders or midfielders.
Using Concer occupies an Arsenal squad slot that could otherwise go to Solace, Odigard or Bay Saka.
He is a strong Wildcard selection but is not yet an essential transfer for managers with a settled defence.

items.headline: Arsenal’s defence leads the GW4 FPL agenda as Cherki and Foden compete for City’s central role
items.summary:
Gameweek 4 arrives with Champions League and Carabao Cup ties still to come, making early transfers riskier than usual despite the temptation to catch price rises. Managers are advised to weigh that risk against any urgent squad issues, particularly with several players carrying uncertain fitness or minutes prospects.

Arsenal’s defensive numbers are the standout early-season FPL story. They have conceded less than 1.0 expected goal across their opening three matches, making their defenders and goalkeeper premium targets, while Zubimendi strengthens his case as a budget midfield option after starting again and completing 90 minutes despite his early Gameweek 2 withdrawal. Honza also makes his first start and registers defensive contributions at £4.4m, offering value if his role holds. By contrast, H has yet to concede an actual goal but has allowed more than 5.0 xG, suggesting that clean-sheet record is vulnerable.

Manchester City’s midfield remains difficult to predict: Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden are expected to share central minutes, limiting both as secure starts. Nico O’Reilly suffers an injury in the warm-up against Coventry, although Enzo Maresca says it does not appear serious. Nathan Collins is a clearer concern after leaving with a calf strain and has no return timeline. Mamedu Sangari also shows he is susceptible to early substitutions, albeit after picking up a yellow card.

Liverpool’s attacking shape offers a possible route into their forwards. When Hugo Ekitike is substituted, Cody Gakpo moves through the middle at number nine, a pattern that may continue. Dominik Szoboszlai begins in midfield before moving to right wing after substitutions and nearly wins a penalty, underlining his attacking involvement. Elsewhere, Diper starts on the left again and appears secure until MTO returns, while Inai is likely to continue playing until Dou is fit, though that return could be imminent. At Nottingham Forest, Munos makes his debut with AA dropping out, which should keep Neco Williams nailed for now.
key_points: Delay non-essential Gameweek 4 transfers until after the Champions League and Carabao Cup matches, as midweek rotation and injuries increase the downside of moving early.
Arsenal are the premier defensive target after allowing under 1.0 xG in three matches, while their opponents’ early clean sheets look less sustainable after conceding more than 5.0 xG.
Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden are expected to share central Manchester City minutes, reducing the security of either midfield pick.
Nathan Collins has a calf strain with no stated return date, making him an injury watch and a potential transfer out.
Cody Gakpo plays as Liverpool’s number nine after Hugo Ekitike goes off, giving him an additional attacking route despite uncertainty over his starting role.
Dominik Szoboszlai’s move from midfield to right wing late on increases his attacking potential, while he nearly wins a penalty.
Neco Williams looks set to remain Nottingham Forest’s secure option after Munos debuts and AA makes way.
Zubimendi completes 90 minutes for Arsenal and Honza records defensive contributions on his first start at £4.4m, though both remain value picks dependent on sustained minutes.

items.headline: Cole Palmer replaces Bruno Fernandes and takes the armband for Hull visit
items.summary:
Cole Palmer becomes the headline move for Gameweek 4 as Bruno Fernandes is sold to target Chelsea’s home fixture against Hull. Palmer is preferred to Morgan Rogers as a short-term explosive option before an intended wildcard in the next couple of weeks, and he is immediately given the captaincy. Hull are yet to concede in the opening three gameweeks, but their underlying numbers are less convincing after allowing more than 5.0 expected goals.

The other confirmed transfers bring Morgan Gibbs-White into midfield in place of Arsenal’s Sol Bamba, despite Bamba returning again. The concern is Bamba’s security of starts, while Gibbs-White offers a more reliable route to minutes. At the back, injured Leeds defender Rodon is upgraded to teammate Muhamed Besic, who is viewed as a useful depth option with attacking potential and a favourable short-term fixture run.

The side lines up in a 3-4-3, with Bart Verbruggen selected in goal ahead of Kinski, although that goalkeeper call is acknowledged as a difficult weekly decision until David Raya can be bought on wildcard. Bryan Mbeumo starts at home to Manchester City ahead of Brighton’s Gomez away at Coventry: Manchester City’s defence has looked vulnerable, while Mbeumo continues to show goal threat. Joao Pedro is vice-captain behind Palmer.
key_points: Cole Palmer replaces Bruno Fernandes and is captained for Chelsea’s Gameweek 4 home match against Hull.
Hull have kept three clean sheets but have conceded more than 5.0 xG, strengthening the case for targeting them with Palmer.
Morgan Gibbs-White arrives for Sol Bamba because Bamba’s minutes appear uncertain despite his recent return.
Injured Rodon is sold for Leeds teammate Muhamed Besic, who adds depth, attacking threat and decent upcoming fixtures.
Bart Verbruggen starts over Kinski in goal, though the position remains unsettled ahead of a planned wildcard for David Raya.
Bryan Mbeumo starts against Manchester City, with Gomez benched for Brighton’s trip to Coventry.
Joao Pedro is named vice-captain in a 3-4-3 setup.
